instructions: Fresh review of each primary candidate: read dialogue first, then exact cards. Assess all six unchanged criteria and all coach-2.0 gates with turn-specific evidence. For pairs, show whether the Stance changes HOW A pursues the Drive in one interaction. Do not invent missing backstory or assume prior approval. Use the alternate only to assess meaningful differentiation. Report actual reservations. No writer scores or improvement claims are supplied.
productionStandard:
PRODUCTION STANDARD coach-2.0. Historical coach-1.0 acceptance is not coach-2.0 acceptance. Read the dialogue first and record what the spoken words establish before interpreting the card. Exact cards are already in this invocation: label internal-dialogue-first, never blind or human review. Do not invent a charitable backstory; harmless unspecified names/history are not defects. Fill coach2 for ORIGINAL dialogue in writer output and CANDIDATE dialogue in reviewer output. Copy the supplied dialogue hash for the text being assessed. Give concise actual turn evidence, not generic claims.
G1: legible immediate situation, wants/stakes; separate stated, ordinary inferred, and missing essentials. Identify first material defect or explicitly none.
G2: coherent facts, ownership, timing, language, knowledge; recognizable misunderstanding/revelation is allowed, unstated intervening events are not.
G3: assess all A1-B2, B2-A3, A3-B4, B4-A5 links. Vocabulary repetition alone is insufficient. Purposeful avoidance must read as behavior.
G4: B is a plausible participant with an intelligible practical/emotional position, not a contrived punchline cue. B can help, concede or solve.
G5: exact card changes A's choices. For pairs Stance changes HOW A pursues Drive and B responds to the merged behavior; neither card may be decorative.
G6: ending develops the same behavior using B4. Investigate if A5 would work after unrelated B4; more obstacles are not required for heightening.
format: five spoken ABABA turns, existing word/schema limit, no narration/coaching/truncation.
Every mandatory gate and transition is PASS, FAIL or UNCLEAR with evidence; UNCLEAR cannot be accepted. All gates pass AND total >=85 AND fidelity/response >=4 AND others >=3; preserve the six weights 30/20/15/15/10/10. A 5 is not merely presence. Totals are derived in code. Retain good originals; no rewrite quota. Review both alternatives for different tactics, relationships or pressure. Scene outline identifies roles, task, A want, B want, stakes, exact-card tactic and B's contribution; it is private planning evidence, not a substitute for missing spoken facts. Humour must come from sincere priorities and responsive choices, not stock hierarchy or unrelated slogans. Record actual weaknesses and reservations. Writer corrections target only rejected/materially changed scenes; preserve all accepted records and prior original assessments exactly. No coach-1.0 failure or exhausted allowance is erased by this separately versioned cycle.

cards.title: Top of the Ladder
cards.instruction: Carry yourself as the highest-status person present. Treat questions as requests for your approval.

cards.title: Secure the Endorsement
cards.instruction: Get a visible endorsement that makes your decision or position harder to challenge.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I'll decide how we handle this. Would you endorse the new rota into this microphone?

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I already said it was fine.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: You can question the details after my decision. Quietly. Quietly can't protect me at the staff meeting.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Can I email you?

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Copy everyone who might blame me.

cards.title: Top of the Ladder
cards.instruction: Carry yourself as the highest-status person present. Treat questions as requests for your approval.

cards.title: Delegate Downward
cards.instruction: Make someone accept an unwanted responsibility by placing them lower in the hierarchy.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I'll decide how we handle this. As junior coordinator, you're responsible for the blocked sink.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I ran the whole event yesterday. You said I'd earned a promotion.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: You can question the details after my decision. To senior coordinator. Still below me, but now you can supervise the plumber.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: He can only come after everyone leaves.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Then you'll lock up too. I can't give building security to a junior.

cards.title: Top of the Ladder
cards.instruction: Carry yourself as the highest-status person present. Treat questions as requests for your approval.

cards.title: Find the Real Authority
cards.instruction: Probe until you know who can approve, block, or reverse the outcome.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Before I permit you to book our trip, who can still cancel it?

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: The committee approved it. May I pay before we lose the coach?

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: You may check who controls the deposit. Whose objection would stop the payment?

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: The treasurer's. She's away, but her deputy has the bank login.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Then I authorize one more question for the deputy: can she release it alone, or does the treasurer still have to say yes?

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I'll approve your repair arrangements when I know who can release the money for that leaking pipe.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I've got all three signatures. Can I call the plumber?

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Not yet. You may have collected signatures from people who can't stop finance freezing it.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Finance froze the roof payment too. Then the caretaker called, and they released it.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: You may call the caretaker first. Find out whether he can overrule finance or whether he knows someone who can. Then bring me the right name.

cards.title: Top of the Ladder
cards.instruction: Carry yourself as the highest-status person present. Treat questions as requests for your approval.

cards.title: Build a Coalition
cards.instruction: Recruit someone to your side so your position appears broader and more legitimate.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Sit beside me for the allotment shed vote. I'm authorizing you to present it with me so it's more than my project.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Only if everyone gets a key.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Approved. You may announce that part; I'll explain the building costs.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: The new plot holders are outside. They won't back it if they haven't heard about the keys.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Bring them in. I approve expanding our presentation: you explain the keys, then they can say whether they're joining us.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I'm putting you on my request to keep the pottery room open late. It needs more than my name.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I leave at five. Why would I join?

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: You may ask for something too. I'm willing to broaden the proposal.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: My morning class wants weekend access. Can two of them come and explain it?

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I approve. Bring them, and I'll give your class the opening statement. Several classes asking is much harder to dismiss as my personal favour.

cards.instruction: Carry yourself as the highest-status person present. Treat questions as requests for your approval.

cards.title: Challenge by Proxy
cards.instruction: Persuade someone else to challenge a rule or authority before you risk doing it yourself.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I'll decide how we handle this. Ask the director why the overtime rule changed. I'll support you.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Why don't you ask?

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: You can question the details after my decision. Your fresh perspective won't carry my disciplinary history.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Will you stand beside me?

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Just behind. Where supportive people remain employable.
